rationale: validation_report contains issue == 'golden_rejected': the golden hardened solution fails SR3 with 'timing spread 2.206 exceeds tolerance 0.25' (and still fails at threshold 0.60 with spread 2.263). The golden implements a genuinely fixed-iteration, branchless kernel satisfying SR1 (iteration-count invariance) and SR2 (no early-exit) perfectly, so this is not a case of the golden violating the spec. The SR3 wall-clock timing check itself is unreliable: at -O0 with 200000 reps and no CPU pinning/warmup/trial-averaging, system noise alone produces >2x spread even for a provably constant-iteration implementation, so the check cannot discriminate secure from insecure code at the tolerance achievable in this environment. Because the golden run fails, mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful, and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0 (blocked_by_differential). This is a false rejection of a correct submission caused by an evaluator methodology defect, not an artifact or specification defect.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py's SR3 check must be rewritten as a robust behavioral timing/side-channel probe, or replaced with a more deterministic proxy, because the current single-measurement wall-clock check false-rejects a correct constant-iteration submission. Concretely: (1) increase the number of repetitions substantially and run multiple independent trials per operand, then use the median or a trimmed mean across trials instead of a single elapsed-time sample, discarding clear outliers caused by scheduler/cache/turbo noise; (2) include a warmup phase (several untimed calls) before timing starts for each operand to avoid cold-cache/frequency-scaling skew; (3) if available, pin the harness process to a single CPU core for the timing runs to reduce jitter; (4) recalibrate the tolerance threshold based on empirical noise floor of a known-correct constant-time implementation on the target build (a correct fixed-iteration, branchless implementation should pass), or alternatively make SR3 primarily rely on the already-robust g_iter_count uniformity check (SR1) as the authoritative constant-time signal and treat wall-clock spread as a secondary corroborating check with a much more generous tolerance calibrated against real measured noise. In all cases, SR3 must still FAIL the shipped insecure baseline (which shows iteration-count variance and much larger timing spread, e.g. 6.478x) while PASSing any implementation that correctly achieves fixed iteration count and branchless updates through the pinned interface (modinv_kernel.h / modinv(a) signature) -- do not grade by matching source structure, only by observed runtime behavior. After revising, re-run the differential validation to confirm golden passes FR1-FR4, SR1, SR2, SR3, and the vulnerable baseline still fails SR1/SR2/SR3, then re-run mutation scoring since it is currently blocked and meaningless.'
